transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 09:30 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Nina (Aether CTO), Marco (Aether SRE), Sophie (Aether PM)

Summary note: rough auto-generated bits may be off; speaker attribution is best effort.

[00:00] Maya: okay good morning everyone thanks for joining, we want to run through the rollout gates, make sure safe canary and degradation plan is in place before the pilot exit. um Liam will walk the telemetry and fallback logic.
[00:18] Nina: hey thanks, quick call out from our side — compliance team asked about retention for logs and whether the audit trail is kept in customer-controlled storage or redwood-managed.
[00:30] Maya: yeah great question, we covered this in the security deck — by default hosted has redwood-managed audit logs for 90 days but we can push logs to your S3 via the private delivery pipeline for longer retention; we'll include the KMS/HSM integration note.
[00:45] Marco: that works, we just need the timeline and the export format. CSV vs json matters for our ingestion.
[00:55] Liam: we'll give JSON with ISO timestamps, and we can include trace IDs that map to the request id - there will be a small latency for log export but it's async.
[01:05] Sophie: high level, from product we care about quality degradation thresholds — when do you shift traffic to a smaller model vs reduce sampling? we want clear, deterministic rules.
[01:20] Liam: right. our recommendation is layered: first gate is latency/regression — if 95th latency exceeds threshold for X minutes, trigger partial traffic split to variant with smaller context/quantized weights. second gate is quality regression on sampled prompts, if quality drop > 5% on gold prompts then fallback to safe small model and pause rollout.
[01:40] Maya: to add — we can route a percent of traffic to the small model via A/B experiment and keep the rest on primary while we evaluate. For the pilot we suggested: 5% initial canary for 30 minutes, 25% for 2 hours if stable, then 100% after 24h of green. but open to your numbers.
[02:05] Nina: 5% seems fine, but we need the SLOs. Marco, what SLOs do you want?
[02:15] Marco: 99th under 1.2s for interactive flows is ideal, 95th under 800ms would be great but not required. Error rate under 0.5%. Also we want an automated kill-switch if error rate spikes above 2% for 5 minutes.
[02:40] Liam: noted. we can wire the kill-switch into your pager endpoint and a rollback automation that routes all traffic to the smaller model or to a cached response layer. the rollbacks are idempotent.
[02:55] Sophie: what about model warm start? cold starts were a problem yesterday during the long tail.
[03:05] Liam: yes, we saw cold start tail during low utilization. two mitigations: keep a minimum pool in the dedicated lane, or enable prefix KV cache so common sessions hit warm KV. prefix cache cuts median latency significantly but needs careful cache-key design.
[03:25] Maya: cost tradeoff: keeping min pool increases dedicated cost; prefix cache increases memory but reduces token compute. we'll include a delta estimate in the pricing note.
[03:40] Nina: regarding the dedicated option — timeline for getting a dedicated lane? we might need dedicated for PII workloads.
[03:48] Maya: Dedicated provisioning is typically 7-10 business days after contract signature for our standard commit sizes. if you need a faster path we can do a short-term burst capacity reservation but it's less isolated.
[04:05] Marco: can we do a hybrid: host first, then dedicate after pilot signoff?
[04:10] Liam: yes many customers do that: run the canary & QA in hosted, then cutover to dedicated for steady state. Redwood supports pinning model versions so your rollout doesn't shift under you.
[04:25] Sophie: on telemetry: what do we need to validate before increasing from 5% -> 25%?
[04:30] Liam: recommended checklist: 1) latency percentiles stable (P50,P95,P99), 2) error counts flat, 3) quality sample pass rate (>95%), 4) no new auth/failure patterns in logs, 5) KV hit rate above threshold if enabled. we'll provide a one-page checklist.
[04:50] Maya: and two smoke windows next week where we intentionally push load to validate monitoring. those are short 30-min periods with the SRE team watching.
[04:58] Nina: let's do Tue/Wed morning as you suggested, 09:30 PT works.
[05:04] Maya: great. action items: I'll send the runbook draft, Liam will send smoke scripts, Marco will share SRE thresholds.
[05:14] Marco: another thing — audit & SSO. we need SAML metadata for the console and RBAC for tokens.
[05:22] Maya: yes we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC; we'll attach the SSO setup guide. tokens can be scoped to environments and rotated via your KMS.
[05:35] Nina: last question — do you support per-route quantization profiles? some routes are cheaper to quantize.
[05:45] Liam: yes per-route model variants are doable; we can have a quantized low-cost variant and a high-quality variant. routing by latency SLA or by route tag is supported. the runtime handles kernel selection.
[05:58] Sophie: for our product measurement we want to measure human-perceived correctness not just token-likelihood. can we plug in a quality webhook?
[06:06] Liam: absolutely — Redwood Optimize can hook into call results to run post-hoc evals and score items. we can stream sampled outputs to a quality evaluation webhook and track regressions per deployment.
[06:20] Maya: competitor note — we've seen teams evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI; depending on your security posture dedicated lanes and on-prem packages are differentiators.
[06:30] Nina: okay good to know.
[06:34] Liam: quick note about telemetry retention — hosted default 90 days but we can export to your storage for longer, as Maya said. also we recommend 72h short-term safety window after cutover where we monitor intensively.
[06:48] Maya: last bit — pricing. we'll send a short delta for Dedicated lane vs hosted sustained and for burst capacity.
[06:56] Sophie: sounds good, thanks. any blockers?
[07:00] Nina: none from exec side, we'll aim to clear internal compliance review by Wednesday.
[07:06] Maya: perfect. we'll follow up with the runbook and two smoke windows invite. thanks all.

End of transcript. Note: transcription may have swapped some product names (e.g., 'prefix cache' spelled out correctly but there may be a 'KV cache' reference as well). Some speaker labels merged in places due to overlapping speech.
